title: Client Seal + Affinity Ledger: optimistic ingest reservation to prevent duplicate billing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Intermittent client/network timeouts + at-least-once ingestion semantics lead to duplicate metered charges when retried requests are accepted and counted by the ingest pipeline. Existing approaches (opaque replay tokens, client-side dedupe windows, server dedupe heuristics) reduce but do not eliminate race conditions across proxies, LB failovers, and multi-region failback. Goal: design and implement a practical, low-latency protocol that prevents duplicate billing in common retry/timeouts without adding large coordination bottlenecks or single-point commits.

Proposal summary: Introduce a short-lived client-generated "seal" (a compact signed token) combined with a per-customer affinity ledger on the ingest frontier. The flow: 1) Client generates a seal per logical request (deterministic nonce + timestamp + client-id) and attaches it as X-Redwood-Seal header; 2) Edge/ingest node attempts an optimistic reservation in the local affinity ledger (idempotent upsert keyed by customer+seal) with state=reserved; 3) The ingest continues through normal pipeline; on success the ingest frontier atomically commits the ledger entry -> state=committed; 4) On transient failure the client retries with the same seal; edge checks the ledger and either returns previous outcome (if committed) or reacquires reservation if previous reservation expired; 5) Periodic reconciliation sweep resolves stale reservations (reserved -> cancelled after TTL + backoff).

Key properties: low-latency (local affinity ledger avoids cross-region sync on the fast path), strong duplicate-suppression for typical retry patterns, bounded memory/disk lifetime via TTL and background sweeps, compatibility fallback for legacy clients (no seal => keep current behavior).

Why this over global sequencer or fully synchronous ledger: global coordination adds end-to-end latency and availability constraints. A local optimistic reservation with deterministic client seal achieves most of the duplicate-suppression benefit with minimal coordination; reconciliation handles rare split-brain cases.

API/SDK changes: add optional X-Redwood-Seal header. SDK helpers to create seals (signed with client SDK key or HMAC using api-key prefix). Provide language-specific helper that produces stable seals for retries. Document header semantics and TTL expectations.
comments: 2026-03-02: Initial write-up and whiteboard session. Decided to favor optimistic local ledger over global sequencing after perf numbers from microbenchmarks (see PR-branch).

2026-03-04: Engineering design review notes: need clear ownership of ledger garbage collection; suggested states: reserved, committed, cancelled, tombstone. Agreed to use a small write-ahead-log per affinity shard for crash-safety.

2026-03-05: Trade-offs discussed with Product (Lara Gomez): P0 because customers have surfaced double-charge incidents. Product asks for a telemetry plan and migration timeline for Dedicated/Private customers.

2026-03-06: Security reviewed basic seal format. Action item: require HMAC using the existing API key secret, and add replay TTL enforcement. Security: avoid exposing per-request HMAC key in logs. See security note: https://confluence.redwood/secure/seal-format (internal).

2026-03-07: Implementation spike: built affinity ledger prototype in rust-edge with local RocksDB store per shard. Benchmarks: median reserve latencies 1.8ms additional on ingest path, p95 ~4.5ms. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge/pull/1832 (prototype).

2026-03-08: Observability plan: add metrics: seal_reserve_attempts, seal_reserve_hits, seal_reserve_conflicts, seal_commit_latency, seal_reconciliation_actions. Dashboards: /dashboards/metering/seal-ledger-overview. Alert: >0.1% unexpected double-counts per 10k requests triggers pager.

2026-03-09: Compatibility: will continue to honor existing dedupe heuristics for legacy clients. SDK rollout: default new SDK versions will enable seals; server will reject malformed seals with 400 and accept without header for opt-out. Backwards-compat path documented in RFC-633 (link: https://docs.redwood/ingest/seals-rfc).

2026-03-10: Migration plan: stage 1 (canary): enable seal support read-path on runtime-1.20 in region us-west-2 for 3 internal customers; stage 2: enable write-path + reconciliation for 50% traffic; stage 3: gradual ramp + customer opt-in. Rollback: feature flag disables seal-reservation atomically.
acceptance_criteria: New header X-Redwood-Seal accepted by edge; idempotent reservation created on affinity ledger for seal key.
Committed ingests with seals result in ledger entries moved to committed within <1s in 99% of cases.
Retries with identical seal do not produce additional meter charges (observed via integration test harness and synthetic workload).
Reconciliation sweep cancels stale reserved entries after TTL and produces audit records for manual review.
Telemetry dashboards and alerts are in place and tested with canary customers.
SDK helpers published for JS/Python/Go and documented examples added to quickstart.
implementation_notes: Affinity ledger sharding: shard by customer-id % N where N = number of leader shards in region; keep shard map small and stable during rollout.
Reservation latency optimization: use local WAL+memtable then background flush; WAL fsync on reserve is optional for performance but required for strict correctness in Dedicated mode (configurable).
Clock skew handling: include client_ts in seal, but rely on server wall time for TTL expiry; accept +/- 5s skew margin to avoid false cancellations.

Quota interactions: reservation consumes a provisional quota unit. If reservation later cancelled, provisional consumption is released. Implement provisional counters namespace to avoid double counting with committed counters.
Backpressure: when affinity shard is overloaded, respond with 429 instructing client to jitter-retry; do not fall back to accepting duplicates silently.
Testing: unit, fuzz tests for seal parsing, chaos tests simulating partition + retries, end-to-end metering verification against golden dataset.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: affinity shard outage causing increased 429s -> mitigation: fast fallback path to best-effort dedupe but alert and auto-scale shards.
Risk: mis-signed/malicious seals may attempt denial-of-service; mitigation: per-customer seal ratelimits and cheap HMAC verification path with token bucket.
Risk: edge storage growth -> mitigation: TTL + aggressive reconciliation + compact tombstone policy, monitor seal-ledger-size metric.
Risk: billing regressions during migration -> mitigation: dual-write shadow ledger and compare counts for 48h, plus manual audit hooks.
